correctness.rationale: Full parameter and graph hypotheses are explicit. The deletion identity gives the universal infeasibility certificate below half and forces uniqueness at equality; a constructive translated graphical zonotope is contained in the core above half. The span of positive-edge differences has rank n-c, while component/complement coalitional bounds give exactly c independent fixed-sum equations, proving matching upper dimension. A separate restricted-game construction proves total balancedness. Degenerate no-positive-arc and endpoint cases are covered. Standalone exact-rational finite checks of 2,555 graph-parameter cases, including all restricted coalition tests and independent rational incidence ranks, passed; these checks are not substituted for universal proof.

originality.rationale: Primary 2024/2026 trust-game results cover the equal-mixing case and total balancedness, and an accessible separate generalized multiset-aggregation insertion theorem implies the total-balancedness direction above half; those implications are not claimed as new. The assessed novel content is (i) impossibility for every nonzero weighted network below half, not merely existence of an obstruction, and (ii) the sharp componentwise affine-dimension n-c law on every network above half. The positive-support component proof and tight translated zonotope inclusion supply those new implications. Exact equivalence/coverage searches showed no matching published theorem, subject to unindexed-literature risk.

value.rationale: The primary 2026 paper expressly identifies mixing weights and determining core stability/uniqueness as a motivated open direction. A theorem applying to every loopless weighted digraph gives an exact existence transition and the precise topology-controlled dimension of stable payoff allocations. Unlike the already known total-balancedness corollary, the every-graph negative law and n-c phase rule answer structural questions for continuous parameters and arbitrarily many network components. The strict-zonotope-inclusion example prevents an unjustified oversimplification of core geometry; full facets and volume remain open.
